_help: Track D: Variety in citing. Items are grouped by stage. See README.md, section 'How to add or edit an item'.
title: Variety in citing

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: Mensah (2022) found that first-year students read more on their phones than on laptops.
items.rule: Author-first (narrative): the author's name is part of the sentence. It puts the focus on who said it.
items.hint: Where is the author's name: in the sentence or in brackets?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: Short study sessions spread across the week help students remember more (Duarte, 2020).
items.rule: Idea-first (parenthetical): the citation is in brackets. It puts the focus on the idea.
items.hint: Where is the author's name: in the sentence or in brackets?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: According to Haddad (2017), bus use often falls when fares rise.
items.rule: Author-first (narrative): the author's name is part of the sentence. It puts the focus on who said it.
items.hint: Is the name part of the sentence?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: Classroom noise can make concentration harder (Abebe, 2016; Pillai, 2020).
items.rule: Idea-first (parenthetical): the citation is in brackets. It puts the focus on the idea.
items.hint: What does the sentence start with: a person or an idea?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: A study by Sato and Kim (2022) showed that students sleep less during exam weeks.
items.rule: Author-first (narrative): the author's name is part of the sentence. It puts the focus on who said it.
items.hint: Is the name part of the sentence?

items.prompt: You want to compare two researchers who disagree with each other. Which pattern fits best?
items.rule: Author-first lets you put the two names side by side: “Haddad (2019) argued …, whereas Moretti (2017) …”.
items.hint: When people disagree, readers need to know who said what.

items.prompt: The idea is widely accepted and several sources support it. You want the focus on the idea, not the people. Which pattern fits best?
items.rule: Idea-first keeps the focus on the idea and can hold several sources in one bracket.
items.hint: Is the person important here, or the idea?

items.prompt: You want to show that a claim is one author's opinion and that you are not fully convinced. Which pattern fits best?
items.rule: Author-first lets you choose a reporting verb (e.g. “Moreau (2019) claimed …”), which shows your stance.
items.hint: Which pattern lets you use a reporting verb?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: As Zhou (2023) {notes|noted}, noise is a common problem in shared student houses.
items.rule: Author-first (narrative): the author's name is part of the sentence. It puts the focus on who said it.
items.hint: Is the name part of the sentence?

items.prompt: Which pattern does this sentence use?
items.frame: Music with lyrics can make reading harder for many students (Kaur & Novak, 2020).
items.rule: Idea-first (parenthetical): the citation is in brackets. It puts the focus on the idea.
items.hint: Where is the author's name: in the sentence or in brackets?

items.prompt: Rewrite this sentence in a new pattern: start with the author's name.
items.frame: Regular online quizzes can improve students' exam results in first-year courses (Castillo, 2021).
modelAnswers: Castillo (2021) found that regular online quizzes can improve students' exam results in first-year courses.
Castillo (2021) {shows|showed} that regular online quizzes can improve students' exam results in first-year courses.
items.rule: Different patterns, same idea: Author (year) argues that … / According to Author (year), … / As Author (year) notes, … / A study by Author (year) found … / … (Author, year).
items.hint: Name first, then the year in brackets, then a reporting verb.

sourceCards.title: Breaks and focus
sourceCards.idea: Short breaks during study help students stay focused.

sourceCards.title: Studying smarter
sourceCards.idea: Students concentrate better when they take regular breaks.

items.prompt: These two sources agree. Write ONE sentence that cites both.
modelAnswers: Regular short breaks help students stay focused (Mwangi, 2019; Tran, 2021).
Both Mwangi (2019) and Tran (2021) found that regular breaks help students concentrate.
items.rule: Two sources that agree: (Adams, 2019; Lee, 2020) in alphabetical order, or Adams (2019) and Lee (2020) both found …
items.hint: In one bracket, which name comes first in the alphabet?
selfCheck: Are both sources cited?
Is the citation format correct (alphabetical order, semicolon, and / &)?
Does my sentence show that the sources agree?
Is the meaning of each source kept?

items.prompt: Every sentence in this paragraph ends with (Author, year). Rewrite two or three sentences so the paragraph has more variety. Then compare with the model.
items.frame: Many students do not get enough sleep during exam weeks (Sato & Kim, 2022). Teenagers who sleep less remember fewer new words (Sato, 2020). Good sleep is linked to higher marks (Nasser et al., 2020). Universities could teach students about sleep in orientation week (Petrova, 2021).
modelAnswers: Many students do not get enough sleep during exam weeks (Sato & Kim, 2022). This matters because, as Sato (2020) {shows|showed}, teenagers who sleep less remember fewer new words. Nasser et al. (2020) also found that good sleep is linked to higher marks. For this reason, Petrova (2021) {suggests|suggested} that universities could teach students about sleep in orientation week.
items.rule: Mix patterns: author-first for people and opinions, idea-first for widely shared facts. Avoid ending every sentence with (Author, year).
items.hint: Try author-first for the findings and for the careful suggestion in the last sentence.
selfCheck: Did I change at least two sentences to a different pattern?
Is every citation still correct (and / &, commas, brackets)?
Does each new verb represent the source fairly?
Is the meaning of each sentence unchanged?

items.prompt: Every sentence in this paragraph ends with (Author, year). Rewrite two or three sentences so the paragraph has more variety. Then compare with the model.
items.frame: Bus use often falls when fares rise (Haddad, 2017). Cheaper fares lead more people to use buses (National Centre for Urban Transport [NCUT], 2021). Bus use also rises when buses come more often (NCUT, 2021). Cities should therefore keep fares low (Moretti, 2017).
modelAnswers: Bus use often falls when fares rise (Haddad, 2017). In a recent report, the National Centre for Urban Transport (NCUT, 2021) found that cheaper fares lead more people to use buses, and that bus use rises when buses come more often. Moretti (2017) therefore {argues|argued} that cities should keep fares low.
items.rule: Mix patterns: author-first for people and opinions, idea-first for widely shared facts. Avoid ending every sentence with (Author, year).
items.hint: The last sentence is an opinion. Which pattern lets you show whose opinion it is?
selfCheck: Did I change at least two sentences to a different pattern?
Is every citation still correct (and / &, commas, brackets)?

items.frame: Plastic bottles are a major source of waste on campus (Ogunleye et al., 2021). Refill stations reduce the number of bottles thrown away (Abebe et al., 2022). Kowalski (2020) goes further and {argues|argued} that every building should have one.
items.rule: Mix patterns: author-first for people and opinions, idea-first for widely shared facts. Avoid ending every sentence with (Author, year).
items.hint: Try “A study by …” for a finding, and author-first for the opinion at the end.

items.prompt: Every sentence in this paragraph ends with (Author, year). Rewrite two or three sentences so the paragraph has more variety. Then compare with the model.
items.frame: Short study sessions help students remember more (Duarte, 2020). Reviewing notes on the same day also improves memory (Varga, 2014, as cited in Osei, 2021). Regular breaks help students stay focused (Tran, 2021). Students should plan short, regular study sessions (Mwangi, 2019).
modelAnswers: Short study sessions help students remember more (Duarte, 2020). Varga (2014, as cited in Osei, 2021) found that reviewing notes on the same day also improves memory. items.frame: Many first-year students skip breakfast (Okafor, 2021). Classes that start early are one reason (Okafor, 2021). Skipping breakfast can make it harder to concentrate in the morning (Pillai, 2020). Universities could offer cheap breakfasts on campus (Petrova, 2021).
